Package com.cognizant.emk.multiagent.infrastructure.mcp

Class McpToolCallbackResolver

java.lang.Object
com.cognizant.emk.multiagent.infrastructure.mcp.McpToolCallbackResolver
@Component public class McpToolCallbackResolver extends Object
Resolves the ToolCallbacks an agent's enabledMcpServers list unlocks, closing the last-mile gap in the OpenAI adapter's MCP wiring (REQ-AGT-009, REQ-MCP-004).

Spring AI's MCP autoconfig publishes a List<McpSyncClient> bean — one client per named stdio connection in spring.ai.mcp.client.stdio.connections.*. The client's client-info name is built by the autoconfig as "<clientName> - <connectionName>" (see McpClientAutoConfiguration.connectedClientName); we correlate back to the yaml connection name by matching each client's suffix against the keys of McpStdioClientProperties.getConnections() snapshotted at startup.

Once the mapping is built, resolve(List) returns exactly the tool callbacks contributed by the requested subset — leveraging SyncMcpToolCallbackProvider so tool-name uniqueness, cache invalidation on McpToolsChangedEvent, and prefix generation stay consistent with Spring AI's built-in behavior.

The provider dependencies are injected via ObjectProvider so every test context that excludes the MCP autoconfig still boots — an absent client bean or an absent properties bean simply yields an empty catalog and every resolve(List) call returns Collections.emptyList().

    • noop

      public static McpToolCallbackResolver noop()
      Test-only factory that returns an instance which resolves every request to an empty callback list — the intent-preserving substitute for the previous "MCPs silently ignored" behavior in tests that do not exercise MCP wiring. Built through the single public constructor with stub ObjectProviders so that Spring's constructor-inference stays unambiguous on the production bean (Spring Boot 4.x's SimpleInstantiationStrategy falls back to a no-arg constructor when a class has multiple declared constructors, so a second private constructor here would cause a startup BeanInstantiationException).

    • resolve

      public List<org.springframework.ai.tool.ToolCallback> resolve(List<String> enabledMcpServers)
      Resolve the tool callbacks contributed by the given enabled MCP servers.

      Unknown names are skipped with a warning — the agent-write-time validator (US-08-006) already rejects unknown MCP names, so a live unknown reference means the catalog changed after the agent was saved, or the autoconfig failed to spawn the client at startup. In either case, degrading gracefully is safer than aborting the turn.
